chapter: The Raeburn band: people and touring
title: The Raeburn audience
summary: The audience depended on venue; Handy imagines Kenton's crowd plus more.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: How much of the audience in those days was--characterize the audience for this band?
It was totally dependent on where we were and what the occasion was. If it was a theater date, we got everybody; if it
was a college date we got the youngsters. If we were out west, we got the people that weren't concerned with jazz.
Did the nature of the music tilt one way or the other? Did you get a more sophisticated jazz crowd or something of a measureable bias, measureable tilt?
Where can you find a sophisticated jazz crowd? I don't recall one ever.
They've got some down in Washington.
No; now. I don't know, in those days they were probably up on 52nd Street, the serious jazz crowds.
I recall that, sure, but it's localized and it's really at a minimum. It probably has enlarged a great deal.
I would think in those days--what I'm trying to describe is Kenton's
crowds would be different than Tommy Dorsey's crowds.
And your crowd, I should think, should be more of the Kenton crowd if not further to the left of the Kenton crowd.
Right. I would think so, exactly.
We would get Kenton's crowd, plus.
